newsitem.title: GERMANY: EMI-Most EU states do not meet conditions for EMU.
newsitem.headline: EMI-Most EU states do not meet conditions for EMU.

text.p: The European Monetary Institute said on Wednesday that budgetary conditions in most European Union member states at the moment do not meet the criteria for the launch of European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
"The report finds, that at the moment a majority of member states do not fulfil the necessary requirements for introducing currency union," the EMI report said.
In a copy of a report on EMU convergence obtained from the Bundesbank, the EMI said that budgetary conditions in most EU states were not yet sustainable in the mid-term.
The Monetary Institute said Germany, France and Italy were among the countries that must make sustained efforts to meet the criteria for joining monetary union.
The EMI,the forerunner to the future European Central Bank, called a stability pact no substitute for convincing budgetary consolidation.
It is responsible for monitoring EU countries' efforts to fulfil the criteria needed to take part in the planned launch of Europe's single currency in 1999.
